title: Unseen: Stealth Sound Effects
shortText: 103 stealth sound effects: detection ladder, distractions, lockpicking, cameras, lasers, alarms, takedowns. WAV + OGG.
html:
The sound of a stealth game's detection ladder, and everything around it

103 stealth sound effects: tension that stacks as suspicion rises, a filling detection meter, escalations and their matched releases, distractions, takedowns, lockpicking, cameras, laser grids and alarms, hiding, light and shadow, guards and 19 seamless loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 24 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. All four tension tiers so you can stack them yourself, an escalation and its release, the same coin on three surfaces, and the lockpick's whole lifecycle.

What is in it

  • Detection (19)
  • Distractions (11)
  • Takedowns (7)
  • Moving quietly (9)
  • Hiding (9)
  • Lockpicking (7)
  • Security (12)
  • Light and shadow (8)
  • Guards (7)
  • Infiltration (9)
  • Places (5)

The detection ladder

Tension is four loops of the same length: tier 1 while the guards are unaware, tier 2 when one grows suspicious, tier 3 while they search, tier 4 when they are alerted. Fade one in per state and the score tightens; every one of the 4 stacks is re-summed from the shipped files and wraps cleanly. The transitions come in matched pairs built as opposites: each escalation builds (its energy sits late in the file) and its release lets go (its energy sits early), measured on the shipped files. A six-step detection meter climbs in brightness as it fills.

Distractions

Throw a coin, a bottle or a stone onto stone, wood or metal, and the surface decides what happens: a coin skitters, dies or rings; a bottle breaks, thuds and rolls, or clangs. Files are named object_on_surface. 9 surface pairs and 9 object pairs measured apart, 0 too close.

Four lifecycles

Lockpick, Security camera, Laser grid, Alarm: each ships its start, a seamless loop while it runs, its stop and the way it fails (the pick snaps, the camera spots you, the beam is broken, the alarm is cut). 16 states, every loop flag read out of the file.

Already own Portcullis or Footfall?

Every one of the 5 roles Unseen shares with Portcullis was measured against it from both packs' files, and each is a different sound. Every one of the 3 roles Unseen shares with Footfall was measured against it from both packs' files, and each is a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 19 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV

loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 4.35 dB.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 958 checks, 0 failed.
  • No voices and nothing musical, so it sits under any score and any cast.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings, and there are no guard voices. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Portcullis: Dungeon Mechanisms, doors, chests, levers and traps as whole lifecycles.
  • Footfall: Footstep Matrix, footsteps on twelve surfaces at four gaits and three weights.
  • Backward: Reversed, Wrong and Uncanny Cues, for when the dark goes wrong.
